changes: Fix: registered channels now get +r, MLOCK and GUARD back when they are recreated after dying or after a restart (services only restored them for channels that already existed when they linked)

Security: with SECUREOPS on, ChanServ strips ops/voice from anyone with no claim to them when a registered channel is recreated, and when services reconnect (channels recreated while services were down no longer keep their creator as op); new registrations have SECUREOPS on by default
Testing: 101 end-to-end integration tests

Security: fixed a use-after-free when a netsplit removed a chain of three or more servers, and IP spoofing through a WebSocket reverse proxy (X-Forwarded-For is now read right-to-left, skipping trusted proxies, instead of trusting the client-supplied leftmost entry)

Client compatibility: usernames like john.doe (the OS login irssi, WeeChat and HexChat send) are cleaned up instead of disconnecting the client; a full-length CAP REQ (gamja, Kiwi, Halloy) is no longer refused; MONITOR lists are split across lines instead of truncated; labeled responses no longer double-tag lines inside CHATHISTORY/multiline batches; STATUSMSG (@#chan) is echoed to echo-message clients; NAMES lines always fit in 512 bytes
New: WHO <mask> (nick, user, host, server, realname; 'o' for opers only), PASS account:password login for clients without SASL, and JOIN 0
Privacy: +i users no longer appear in WHO masks or in WHO #channel for people outside the channel

Fixes: RENAME keeps the channel's chat history; cap-notify sends correct SASL values (EXTERNAL when available, bare names to pre-302 clients); read markers and STATS m counters are bounded correctly; web chat nick fallback can no longer stall registration
Testing: 98 end-to-end integration tests (10 new client-compatibility tests)

Multi-server networking: SekurIRCd servers now link into a tree and share users, channels, modes, topics, bans, messages, away/account/host state and G-lines, with TS-based channel merging, nick-collision resolution, netsplit QUITs, /MAP, /LINKS, /SQUIT (also remote), /CONNECT, KILL/WALLOPS/GLOBOPS across servers and ChanServ serving users on any server. links.mode "both" with several [[links.peers]] and links.autoconnect
Accounts are replicated between linked servers (register, password, email, grouped nicks, drop; sent in the burst, last writer wins)

IRCv3: CAP 302/cap-notify, msgid, TAGMSG, batch, labeled-response, chathistory (server-level store with optional persistence and DM history), draft/multiline, draft/read-marker, draft/channel-rename, draft/no-implicit-names, draft/pre-away, extended-monitor, SASL SCRAM-SHA-256

Channel modes +f, +j, +L, +D, +u, +G, +q/+a ranks (~ and &); extbans ~r, ~z, ~j; caller-ID (+g/ACCEPT); connection classes; WEBIRC; PROXY protocol v1/v2; WebSocket (ws/wss) listener; oper privilege classes, SHUN, ELINE, GLOBOPS, SANICK, CHGIDENT, TESTLINE, LOCOPS, USERIP

NickServ: SET PASSWORD, DROP, LOGOUT, INFO, SET EMAIL/VERIFY, GROUP/UNGROUP, GHOST and nick enforcement. ChanServ: account-based founder, SECUREOPS, RESTRICTED, PRIVATE, LIST, extended MLOCK, owner/admin ranks

Hardening from the 2026-10 audit (stale worker results, link allowed_ips, +P abuse, NOTICE auto-replies, ISUPPORT/protocol fixes, link/worker robustness) and rehash now rebinds listeners and reloads the TLS certificate
Testing: 88-test end-to-end integration suite (make itest, including 3-server networks), clean under ASan/UBSan, plus a parser fuzz harness (make fuzz)

Security audit: fixed a TLS handshake busy-loop DoS, umode +q (unkickable) being settable by any user instead of opers only, a proxy-scanner flood/cap-limit bypass, and hostname K/G-lines and channel bans that silently never matched (rDNS result and bans now check the real host/IP, not just a possibly-cloaked displayed one)
Security: new per-IP throttle on SASL/NickServ IDENTIFY, a timing-safe decoy for unknown accounts, and a fix for a second login attempt applying its result to the wrong pending account
Security: /REGISTER's instant self-service account creation no longer grants full spam-check exemption immediately; accounts.json/klines.json are now written 0600 with fsync-before-rename
Bugfix: use-after-free on self-KICK/SAPART, case-only nick changes never being announced, and SAJOIN/auto_join handing out ops on a channel it didn't actually create

ChanServ: SUCCESSOR CLAIM now checks a claimant's real identity over the link instead of the (possibly cloaked) PRIVMSG sender host, so a hostmask or "=account" successor actually works; identified-founder state now expires and is cleared on DROP/reconnect instead of occasionally sticking forever and permanently blocking a legitimate CLAIM; AKICK now also sets a ban; several crash/data-loss fixes in the JSON store
New channel modes +R (registered-only join), +O (oper-only join), +M (registered/voice+ only speak), +c (reject colour/formatting outright)
New quiet extban m:/~m: (blocks speaking, not joining); ~a: alias for the existing a:account extban; /LIST now matches a #-prefixed pattern and a leading ! negates
New ChanServ commands: OP/DEOP/VOICE/DEVOICE/HALFOP/DEHALFOP, INVITE, UNBAN, KICK, TOPIC
New IRCv3 STS support ([tls] sts_duration)

Performance: O(1) worker-result lookup (was O(n) per result, O(n^2) across a connect burst) and a send buffer that shrinks back down after a large burst instead of staying at its peak size for the connection's life

New Protection bundle: an optional, one-file abuse-protection layer (config/protection.toml, template in config/protection.template.toml) that groups DNSBL blacklists, the new proxy scanner, connection limits, the connect-flood throttle, the per-client flood guard and spam protection. Leave the file out and nothing changes

Active open-proxy scanner ([scanner], off by default): on connect the server tries HTTP CONNECT, HTTP POST, SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 back through the client's own address to its own public address; a working relay bans the address and drops everyone connected from it. Runs in the background on non-blocking sockets in the main loop, with a per-probe timeout, a concurrency cap and an optional negative cache

DNSBL blacklists moved into the bundle ([blacklist]) and gained per-zone reply rules: exact or bitmask reply codes, ban_unknown, and a per-zone ban reason with %i/%t/%r placeholders. The old [dnsbl] section keeps working and logs a deprecation warning

Connection caps, the connect-flood throttle, the flood guard and [spam] can now live in the bundle file ([connection], [flood], [spam]); where the bundle sets a key it overrides sekurircd.toml, and the old keys still work
[exempt] lists IP globs that are never DNSBL-checked or scanned; connections a scan relays back to the server are exempt from the connect-flood throttle and per-IP cap
New oper command /PROTECT shows the bundle's state and counters; /PROTECT SCAN <ip> scans an address on demand. /VERSION shows a P flag for the scanner
Bundle activity is logged with the protection/dnsbl tags and relayed into your debug channel: bans, a startup/REHASH summary and the periodic stats line now include proxy-scanner counters
A DNSBL hit now also disconnects every other connection from that address; the server sends the standard NOTICE AUTH "*** Looking up your hostname" line on connect
Docs: new Protection bundle page and config template
Security: fixed a remotely-triggerable stack buffer overflow in channel MODE handling, reachable by any channel operator
Security: ident/rDNS/DNSBL lookups are now bounded by their configured timeouts (dnsbl.timeout and rdns_timeout were previously ignored) and can no longer stall the worker pool
Security: bans, /SILENCE and ChanServ ACCESS/AKICK now match identd-confirmed users correctly; a mask written the way WHOIS displays a user finally bites
KLINE/GLINE now match host and user@host masks, not just IPs; ZLINE stays IP-only for connect-time bans
Security: constant-time password comparison for OPER/DIE/RESTART and server links; hardened build flags (stack protector, FORTIFY_SOURCE, RELRO/BIND_NOW on Linux)
INVITE can no longer be used to send arbitrary text around /SILENCE, +D and +R
Fixed an out-of-descriptors condition that pegged a CPU core, and a lost auth result that permanently wedged a connection's ability to log in
/REGISTER is rate-limited and the account store is capped ([accounts] max_accounts)
Config validation no longer overflows on a bad host_masking_token_bytes; max_params, max_nick_length and max_message_length are range-checked
Performance: O(1) per-IP connection counting, deduplicated and batched K-line writes, debounced ChanServ store writes
A leaf server reconnect no longer freezes the event loop for the OS connect timeout
SASL EXTERNAL: log in with a TLS client certificate, bound with /CERT ADD
Z-lines (ZLINE/UNZLINE), /WATCH, and STATS k/g/z/l
Per-IP connect-flood throttle that auto-bans scanners
Server-notice (+s) alerts for OPER, failed OPER, KILL, links, and SA*/SETHOST overrides
Optional oper host masking on /OPER, human-friendly ban expiry and uptime
Rootless systemd user units, make install/uninstall, and a start/stop/status wrapper script
Hardened server-link listener; random RPL_YOURID
New /RULES command backed by config/ircd.rules, and an operator MOTD (config/oper.motd) sent on /OPER and via /OPERMOTD; both reload on /REHASH
New [messages] keys: oper_motd and rules; templates for both files are included

New spam protection module ([spam], off by default): regex content filters for PRIVMSG/NOTICE (users and channels) plus AWAY, QUIT, PART and TOPIC text; a new-connection restriction on PMs; and recipient/repeat limits that catch bots messaging many targets
Filters live in config/spamfilters.conf (an example file is included) with actions block, warn, kill and zline; filters_enabled turns the file off without touching the rest
New /SPAMFILTER LIST|ADD|DEL oper command edits the filters file live; regexes are validated (no backreferences, no empty matches); rules reload on /REHASH
Opers with +s get a notice for every spam action, and services, opers and identified accounts are exempt by default

/VERSION is now ircu/solanum-style: SekurIRCd-<version>(<date>-<commit>) plus feature flags and the full 005 ISUPPORT list; WHOX and MAXCHANNELS are now advertised, and 004 carries the same build string

Accounts: IRCv3 draft/account-registration (REGISTER <account|*> <email|*> <password>) and a built-in NickServ (REGISTER / IDENTIFY) alongside /REGISTER and SASL; registering while already logged in is now refused
User mode +B marks a client as a bot (IRCv3 bot mode): 335 in WHOIS, B in WHO flags, @bot message tag, BOT=B in 005
Periodic stats server notice for opers
ChanServ bug fixes
README rewritten as a standalone project doc
Fixed crashes, security holes and performance stalls; wired up previously dead config options
New channel and user modes: +P +C +T +S +V +Q +N
Fixed the Linux build (glibc POSIX gating) and added a TLS connect notice
Expanded ChanServ HELP; fixed OPER re-auth and TOPICLOCK sync; WHOX support
Initial release of the C port
